description: Puzzles are a crucial part of Logical Reasoning where given jumbled information must be arranged in a systematic order. It involves connecting various variables based on their given characteristics.

sections.title: Main Types of Puzzles
sections.description: Puzzles in exams can be categorized into various types based on the variables and parameters involved.

key_concepts.explanation: Arranging persons or objects on different floors of a building. The lowermost floor is usually considered as 1.
Placing different boxes one above the other in a stack. It does not have a fixed base.
Arranging events or persons according to days of the week, months, or years.

sections.title: Floor and Box Based Puzzles
sections.description: These puzzles require creating a vertical arrangement where keeping track of top and bottom positions is essential.

key_concepts.explanation: Place definite information directly into the main table. Write negative information outside the table with a cross.

results: A and B will be on consecutive floors.
A's floor number = B's floor number + 1

cases.condition: There are two boxes between A and B
results: Box A can be above and B below, or vice-versa.
Possibilities: A _ _ B or B _ _ A

sections.title: Scheduling and Day/Month Based Puzzles
sections.description: Arrangement is done according to a time cycle. Days or months are always taken as a fixed base.

key_concepts.explanation: It is important to remember which months have 30 days (e.g., April, June) and which have 31 days.
Always make days (Monday to Sunday) or months (January to December) the left column or base of your table.

cases.condition: A goes in a month having less than 30 days
results: A will only go in February.
Check the nature of the year (Normal or Leap year).

sections.title: Important Connecting Words
sections.description: Understanding the exact meaning of specific words used in puzzles is crucial for accuracy.

results: Sentence: 'A is above B and below C.'
Here 'And' refers to the first person, i.e., 'A'. (C > A > B)
Sentence: 'A is above B who is below C.'
Here 'Who' refers to the immediately preceding person, i.e., 'B'.

sections.title: Steps to Solve Puzzles
sections.description: Adopting a systematic and logical approach to solve puzzles is important to save time.

steps.title: Identify the Base
steps.detail: Read the given information and choose a fixed variable (like days, months, floors, or years) around which other information will be arranged.

steps.title: Draw a Table
steps.detail: Draw a clean table with the base variable. Keep a separate column for negative constraints.

steps.title: Enter Definite Information
steps.detail: Find the information from the paragraph that is 100% true and direct, and write it directly into the table. Write indirect info in the rough.

steps.title: Create Possibilities/Cases
steps.detail: If any information can fit in more than one place, create parallel cases. As you read further, wrong cases will automatically be eliminated.
